issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes issue requesting that decimal exponential form be allowed in all formats, including XML as an xs:decimal/xs:double union so values such as 1.00E3 can preserve significant digits.
initial_application: The Jira comment says the issue was applied in svn revision 13843, which maps to git commit c8e08d05ceadfdcd439fa409adf52bf0efecffe4. That commit removed the old exponent prohibition from datatypes.html and updated primitives.xml. Same-day companion commit 79c1c0b5cb433f8068e231bd3ab2378464654f41 updated XML guidance and search-number examples for exponent-capable decimals.
additional_context: Current combined source keeps the exponent-capable decimal rule in active pages and datatype sources: datatypes.html, primitives.xml, xml.html, rdf.html, and history.html are consistent with the issue. The relevant Zulip thread confirms presentation-form preservation, INF/NaN exclusion, XML decimal/double union handling, and search implications. Related decimal precision issues FHIR-5653 and FHIR-8175 do not reverse this policy.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current source already allows decimal exponential form and no checked source still carries the old exponent prohibition.
